# osc_access_token (Resource)

Manages a fine-grained access token: a token for one workspace whose permissions are a policy kept by the platform, not in the token. Use it for CI, agents and other automation that should hold less than a full personal access token. Create it from a `template` or an explicit `policy`.

The token value is returned by the platform once, when the token is created. It is exposed as the sensitive attribute `token` and stored in the Terraform state, so protect the state (use an encrypted remote backend). The expiry of a token cannot be extended: to rotate it, run `terraform apply -replace=osc_access_token.<name>`.

The policy, name, description, status and enforcement change in place and the token value stays the same. A change of `template` or `expires_in_days` replaces the token.

Creating tokens is not enabled in every environment yet; where it is not, creating the resource fails with an error saying so.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A token for CI that can only read: made from a template, valid for 30 days.
resource "osc_access_token" "ci_viewer" {
  name            = "ci-viewer"
  description     = "Read-only token for the CI pipeline"
  template        = "viewer"
  expires_in_days = 30
}

# A token with an explicit policy. Changing the policy later keeps the same token
# value; it is replaced in place.
resource "osc_access_token" "deployer" {
  name = "release-deployer"
  policy = jsonencode({
    version = 1
    statements = [
      {
        actions   = ["myapps:read", "myapps:deploy"]
        resources = ["myapps/*"]
      }
    ]
  })
}

# The token value is stored in the Terraform state, so protect the state. To rotate
# the token, run: terraform apply -replace=osc_access_token.deployer
output "deployer_token" {
  value     = osc_access_token.deployer.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the token, shown in the console and in audit events. Changed in place.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the token is for. Changed in place.
- `enforcement` (String) `enforce` or `audit`. With `audit` the platform records what the policy would have refused but allows it. Defaults to `enforce`. Changed in place.
- `expires_in_days` (Number) Lifetime of the token in days, 1 to 90. Omitted means 90. The expiry is fixed when the token is created, so changing this replaces the token.
- `policy` (String) The policy of the token as a JSON string, normally `jsonencode(...)`: `{"version": 1, "statements": [{"actions": ["myapps:read"], "resources": ["myapps/*"]}]}`. Set exactly one of `template` and `policy`. A change replaces the policy of the same token in place, guarded by `policy_version`: if the policy was changed outside Terraform since it was last read, the apply fails and a new plan is needed. A policy that means the same as the stored one, such as one with other formatting, changes nothing. A policy cannot give more permissions than the caller of the API has.
- `status` (String) `active` or `disabled`. A disabled token is refused by the platform until it is activated again. Defaults to `active`, and a new token is always created active, so a change that replaces the token (`template` or `expires_in_days`) cannot also set `disabled`: apply it first, then disable the token. Changed in place.
- `template` (String) A named policy the platform expands into a policy when the token is created: one of `viewer`, `deployer`, `ci-publisher`, `agent-runner`, `mcp-readonly` or `full`. Set exactly one of `template` and `policy`. The template is not stored as a reference, so changing it replaces the token. To change the scope of the same token, use `policy`: replacing `template` with `policy` in the configuration replaces the policy of the existing token in place.

### Read-Only

- `effective_policy` (String) The policy as the platform stores it, as normalised JSON. For a token created from a template it is the policy the template expanded to.
- `expires_at` (String) When the token expires (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) The token id (`patId`). Use it with `terraform import`.
- `last_used_at` (String) When the platform last saw the token used (RFC 3339), refreshed on every read. Null while it has not been used.
- `policy_version` (Number) Version of the stored policy, raised by every policy change.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token value, to use as an OSC access token. The platform returns it only when the token is created, so it is stored in the Terraform state and a read never changes it: protect the state, for example with an encrypted remote backend. It is null for an imported token, because the value cannot be read back. The expiry cannot be extended: to rotate the token, run `terraform apply -replace=osc_access_token.<name>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a token by its id (`osc token list` shows it). The token value cannot be
# read back, so `token` stays null; the template and the lifetime are not known
# either, so describe the token with `policy`.
terraform import osc_access_token.deployer 0b6f1c2e-5d1a-4f7e-9a1c-2f3d4e5a6b7c
```
